heading: If you or someone you love is pregnant
intro: Most of these deaths come from problems that can be caught and treated: high blood pressure, heavy bleeding and infection. Knowing the danger signs and getting to a facility that can act quickly saves lives.

heading: If you work in maternity care
intro: The killers are clustered and predictable - eclampsia in younger women, haemorrhage in older ones, sepsis alongside abortion. Readiness for those three emergencies matters most, and anaemia and heart disease deserve attention too.

heading: If you shape maternal health policy
intro: Direct causes drive most deaths, but their mix is shifting toward haemorrhage and cardiovascular disease. Investment in blood supplies, emergency obstetric care and routine use of hospital data would target the trend.
